narrative.coaching_note: Clean your hands with alcohol rub or soap and water at 8.1 seconds after touching bed rail A and call button and before touching phone. You touched bed rail A at 1.6 seconds with your bare hand, and that moved contamination to your hand. Alcohol rub works against MRSA, so use it or soap and water before the next touch. You then touched call button at 7.6 seconds and phone at 8.1 seconds, which carried it to both of those objects. You later touched resident A at 21.4 seconds, which carried it to resident A. Cleaning your hands before touching resident A at 21.4 seconds was also needed. Cleaning your hands at 8.1 seconds would have kept clean your bare hand and gloved hand and phone and resident A.
narrative.audit_summary: MRSA source was bed rail A. Bare hand touched bed rail A at 1.6 seconds, transferring contamination to bare hand, then to call button at 7.6 seconds, to phone at 8.1 seconds, and to resident A at 21.4 seconds, with one exposure of resident A. Missed Moment 5 at 8.1 seconds and Moment 1 at 21.4 seconds. Hand hygiene compliance was 0/2 overall, with Moment 1 at 0/1 and Moment 5 at 0/1. No hygiene events occurred. No glove use issue was noted. Alcohol rub and soap and water are effective against MRSA. Contaminated at end were bare hand, gloved hand, bed rail A, call button, phone, and resident A. Disinfect phone, bed rail A, call button, and resident A with Use an EPA List H registered disinfectant (effective against MRSA).
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was hand hygiene at 8.1 seconds.
